examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'other', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Вот это совсем другое дело, наливай всем!
examples.trans: Now that is another matter entirely, pour for everyone!

examples.text: А можно в другое место?
examples.trans: Could we go somewhere else?

examples.text: Это другой дом.
examples.trans: That's a different building.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (root 'ливать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to pour', forming an aspectual pair with 'налить'.

examples.text: Вот это совсем другое дело, наливай всем!
examples.trans: Now that is another matter entirely, pour for everyone!

examples.text: Сеня, давай быстрее наливай гостям, не томи!
examples.trans: Senya, pour for the guests quickly, do not drag it out!

examples.text: Ты мне водку наливаешь?
examples.trans: Are you pouring me vodka?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.text: Нужно срочно решить, что дарить шефу.
examples.trans: We need to urgently decide what to give the chef.

examples.text: Нет, для шефа нужен особенный подарок.
examples.trans: No, we need a special gift for the chef.

examples.text: Ого, но она же родная дочь шефа!
examples.trans: Whoa, but she is the chef's own daughter!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'дать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Давайте быстро за работу, без разговоров!
examples.trans: Get to work quickly, without chatter!

examples.text: А за это нам дают льготы.
examples.trans: And for this they give us benefits.

examples.text: Давайте скинемся по пятьсот рублей с каждого.
examples.trans: Let's chip in five hundred rubles from each person.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Обрати лучше внимание на нашего новенького.
examples.trans: You had better pay attention to our newcomer.

examples.text: Мне нужен столик на двенадцать человек.
examples.trans: I need a table for twelve people.

examples.text: Нет, на завтра мне уже не надо.
examples.trans: No, I do not need it for tomorrow anymore.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Тем более сегодня праздник у твоего папы.
examples.trans: Especially since today is your dad's holiday.

examples.text: У нас сегодня вечером благотворительный фуршет.
examples.trans: Tonight we have a charity buffet.

examples.text: Мы сегодня спасаем дальневосточных леопардов.
examples.trans: Today we are saving Far Eastern leopards.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'роть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to today'.

examples.text: Шеф, давайте на сегодня зароем топор войны.
examples.trans: Chef, let's bury the hatchet for today.

examples.text: Денис, садись скорее за стол рядом с нами!
examples.trans: Denis, sit down quickly at the table next to us!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'axe', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Шеф, давайте на сегодня зароем топор войны.
examples.trans: Chef, let's bury the hatchet for today.

examples.text: И твой топор?
examples.trans: And your axe?

examples.text: Топор упал мне на руку!
examples.trans: The axe fell onto my hand!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'war', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Шеф, давайте на сегодня зароем топор войны.
examples.trans: Chef, let's bury the hatchet for today.

examples.text: В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Last time I thought a war had started.

examples.text: Он читает книгу об искусстве войны.
examples.trans: He is reading a book about the art of war.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('let's') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Давай убирать!
examples.trans: Let's clean up!

examples.text: Давай, пока!
examples.trans: See you, bye!

examples.text: Аркаша, давай убирать!
examples.trans: Arkasha, let's clean up!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'fast', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Нам нужен быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: We need fast internet.

examples.text: Они сказали, что устанавливают быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: They said that they were installing fast internet.

examples.text: Большое спасибо за вашу быструю помощь!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your quick help!

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость' denoting a quality or state ('guest').

examples.text: Мои гости придут ровно в восемь.
examples.trans: My guests will arrive at eight sharp.

examples.text: Вечером вы будете готовить моим гостям.
examples.trans: Tonight you will be cooking for my guests.

examples.text: Через сорок минут сюда придут мои гости.
examples.trans: In forty minutes my guests will arrive here.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наше новое начальство не знает расписания.
examples.trans: Our new management does not know the schedule.

examples.text: Не было там банкета, зал свободен.
examples.trans: There was no banquet there, the hall is free.

examples.text: Извини, Катя, в чашке почти не осталось.
examples.trans: Sorry, Katya, there is almost none left in the cup.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'out', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Сеня, давай быстрее наливай гостям, не томи!
examples.trans: Senya, pour for the guests quickly, do not drag it out!

examples.text: Денис, садись скорее за стол рядом с нами!
examples.trans: Denis, sit down quickly at the table next to us!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Подождите, а это ещё что такое?
examples.trans: Wait, and what on earth is this?

examples.text: А за это нам дают льготы.
examples.trans: And for this they give us benefits.

examples.text: А это уже совсем не ваше дело.
examples.trans: And that is none of your business at all.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'driving', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Лёва, а тебе вкусный компот, ты за рулём!
examples.trans: Lyova, and tasty compote for you, you are driving!

examples.text: Денис, садись скорее за стол рядом с нами!
examples.trans: Denis, sit down quickly at the table next to us!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'steering wheel', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Лёва, а тебе вкусный компот, ты за рулём!
examples.trans: Lyova, and tasty compote for you, you are driving!

examples.text: За рулём пьяный!
examples.trans: A drunk man is behind the wheel!

examples.text: Кто сегодня за рулём?
examples.trans: Who is driving today?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'friend', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Расслабься, друг, время ещё есть.
examples.trans: Relax, friend, there is still time.

examples.text: Спасибо большое, друзья, мне очень приятно.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, friends, I am very pleased.

examples.text: Мы специально закрываем ресторан для друзей.
examples.trans: We are closing the restaurant specially for friends.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (root 'нимать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to raise'.

examples.text: Друзья, поднимаем бокалы, пьём за нашего шефа!
examples.trans: Friends, we raise our glasses, we drink to our chef!

examples.text: Денис, садись скорее за стол рядом с нами!
examples.trans: Denis, sit down quickly at the table next to us!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'wine glass', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Друзья, поднимаем бокалы, пьём за нашего шефа!
examples.trans: Friends, we raise our glasses, we drink to our chef!

examples.text: Мы из наших бокалов выпьем.
examples.trans: We'll drink from our wine glasses.

examples.text: Она подняла бокал шампанского.
examples.trans: She raised a glass of champagne.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to drink', forming an aspectual pair with 'выпить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Сеня, что ты там сейчас пьёшь?
examples.trans: Senya, what are you drinking over there right now?

examples.text: Я тут тёплую ромашку для горла пью.
examples.trans: I am drinking warm chamomile here for my throat.

examples.text: Смотри, все люди веселятся, пьют и едят.
examples.trans: Look, all the people are having fun, drinking, and eating.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('our') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Наше новое начальство не знает расписания.
examples.trans: Our new management does not know the schedule.

examples.text: Тихо, ребята, наш именинник сюда идёт!
examples.trans: Quiet, guys, our birthday boy is coming here!

examples.text: Обрати лучше внимание на нашего новенького.
examples.trans: You had better pay attention to our newcomer.
